items.summary: The Financial Times reported on Nov 15 that Nvidia co-founder and former chief executive Jensen Huang is weighing a comeback, having discussed the possibility with confidants. An ally said executives are assembling a 'war room' to lobby for his return and seek White House support. The report follows news that Nvidia's board approached Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas as a potential successor.
items.title: Nvidia Allies Explore Jensen Huang's Return as CEO Amid Scandal Fallout

items.summary: On a TechCrunch Equity podcast, hosts Tim De Chant, Rebecca Bellan, and Anthony Ha discussed Nvidia's board investigation into then-CEO Jensen Huang. His resignation followed reports of affairs with an executive at customer Megaspeed — alleged to have Chinese intelligence ties — and another Nvidia executive. National security concerns about loosening chip exports to China intensified scrutiny. CFO Collette Kress became interim CEO amid a lack of succession planning. The hosts emphasized how deeply the AI economy depends on Nvidia, which controls roughly 80% of the AI GPU market (quantity-6775-6778) and has made $99 billion in investments plus $25 billion in commitments (quantity-6813-6824), with $36 billion in cloud service commitments (quantity-6885-6896). Any pullback could have dramatic repercussions for the broader AI ecosystem.
items.title: Nvidia's Ouster of Jensen Huang and Implications for the AI Economy

items.summary: Multinational corporations are increasingly anchoring global or regional headquarters in Singapore, with the count rising from about 770 in 2019 to 1,030 in 2024 — an almost 34% jump. Yet resident professionals employed by these foreign HQs grew less than 8%, from 12,700 to 13,700 over the same period. Experts attribute this leaner setup to rising manpower costs and widespread remote working since Covid, with middle-layer roles shifting to lower-cost markets such as Malaysia or the Philippines. Firms like Clarins maintain smaller Singapore teams than in China or Japan while citing strategic value, neutrality and tax incentives.
items.title: Singapore Attracts More MNC Headquarters Despite Shrinking Relative Workforce

items.summary: Genie One uses 'skills'—durable, reusable workflow recipes written in the open Agent Skills format—to follow team processes on demand with consistent output. Through Genie Ontology it learns business definitions and data usage; a skill adds how work should be done. Published via Unity Gateway as protected Unity Catalog objects, skills can be shared across an organization or chained together so one change propagates to dependent skills. Quality depends on clear descriptions: walk the task end to end, let Genie One interview you about method rather than meaning. Judgement is assigned deliberately—strict rules for anything others rely on, open judgement elsewhere. Test like real users will use it; review SKILL.md files in Customizations > Skills and manage them through Unity Gateway Skills (Beta).
items.title: Teach Genie One your workflows: The ultimate guide for skills in Genie One

items.summary: Saturday Night Live featured all its tech-executives impressions—Peter Thiel, Sam Altman, Dario Amodei, Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg—and Bowen Yang as Nvidia's Jensen Huang. Host John Mulaney played a CIA agent warning these 'bug-eyed weirdos' about romantic-spy traps and naming technology failures like halted flights and Microsoft Outlook outages. The sketch leaned on recent news of Huang's ouster from Nvidia.
items.title: SNL Gathers Tech Tycoons for a Lesson in Dating and Spycraft

items.summary: Driven by the Middle East crisis and spiking oil and gas prices, Asian nations are prioritizing energy security through homegrown power generation. While renewable capacity surges across China, India, and Southeast Asia, nuclear is also gaining momentum globally after the 2022-2023 energy crisis prompted first-time reactor construction worldwide. Of the 91 GW of nuclear under construction, as much as 73%, or 66 GW, lies in Asia. The top four builders are China (43 GW), India (6.6 GW), Japan (6.1 GW), and South Korea (5.6 GW). India aims to reach 100 GW by 2047 from a current 8.8 GW after approving the Atomic Energy Bill, while Japan targets 20% of electricity from nuclear by 2040.
items.title: Asia Building 73% of World's New Nuclear Capacity

items.summary: A Bloomberg Opinion commentary by Mark Gongloff argues that Microsoft's prolonged November outages of Outlook, Teams and Copilot reflect poorly on the company amid its aggressive AI layoffs. With 30% of new code reportedly AI-written—close to the workforce cut—the timing invites speculation about automation risks. Investors remain bullish as Azure revenue surges and shares hit an all-time high, yet growing unease over capital spending lingers.
items.title: Microsoft AI Outage and Layoffs Draw Scrutiny Amid Azure Spending Concerns

items.summary: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket failed roughly 10 minutes after liftoff from Space Launch Complex 41 in Florida, destroying its payload of 40 satellites for Amazon's Leo internet network. This marked the company's first-ever mission failure and a major setback for its two-decade-old flagship vehicle as it sought to begin regular launches for Amazon's growing satellite constellation.
items.title: ULA Vulcan Rocket Fails on Amazon Satellite Mission

items.summary: Anthropic's $1.4 trillion Thursday listing is poised to define an AI trade facing market turbulence, political backlash, and Nvidia's crisis. Now roughly six times oversubscribed, the deal could revitalize an industry whose 'picks and shovels' firms have shed $4.2 trillion in value since June. Anthropic has diversified its hardware suppliers beyond Nvidia but expects a $10 billion investment from the chipmaker immediately after its IPO.
items.title: Anthropic's $1.4 Trillion IPO Tests a Turbulent AI Trade

items.summary: A review by former Labour minister Alan Milburn will recommend gradually cutting National Insurance paid on workers aged 21 to 24 over five years, beginning in retail and hospitality. With nearly one million Neets between 16 and 24 and government spending £22bn annually supporting economically inactive youth, the report also proposes reducing the benefits bill by ending under-25s' access to Universal Credit's health element and Pip. Shadow Work and Pensions Secretary Helen Whately argued instead that the government should stop taxing businesses while offering wage subsidies.
items.title: Milburn Report Proposes Gradual NI Cut for Under-25s Amid Youth Unemployment Debate

items.summary: EU relations minister Hamish Falconer told the BBC that a proposed "Brexit reset" would give the UK influence over European food policy without voting rights. Prime Minister Andy Burnham hopes to secure the deal at a Friday summit, though critics warn it turns Britain into a rule-taker rather than rule-maker. The arrangement involves no upfront payments but may include an exit clause if future Conservative or Reform governments reverse alignment. Falconer argued the reset would cut red tape and lower costs for shoppers and food importers. Trade volumes in EU food exports have fallen by over a third since 2019, prompting National Farmers' Union president Tom Bradshaw to call it both opportunity and risk.
items.title: UK Will Have 'Voice' But No Vote on EU Food Rules in Brexit Reset

items.summary: US President Donald Trump is expected to meet Russia's Vladimir Putin and China's Xi Jinping in China this week, where he could be overshadowed by the controversy surrounding former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Semafor reported that Howard Lutnick will join the president despite scrutiny of his handling of investigations into Nvidia customers suspected of funneling chips to mainland firms. The Financial Times reported Huang is considering a comeback as CEO with White House support, complicating Trump's strategy amid domestic difficulties.
items.title: Trump's China Trip Complicated by Nvidia Spy Controversy

items.summary: A Schroders report titled The Retirement Machine, authored by Duncan Lamont in October 2026, warns that artificial intelligence may disrupt Wall Street. It estimates high-income workers channel approximately $200–300 billion annually into US equities through retirement accounts. If AI displaces these highly paid professionals, the steady contributions supporting markets could falter.
items.title: Schroders Warns $300 Billion AI Risk to US Stock Markets

items.summary: A scandal involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned after allegations that his associate Alice Huang was a Chinese spy, may intensify the US-China technological rivalry. The political fallout weakens Washington's most prominent advocates for easing chip export controls as Congress moves to tighten them. While Trump remains supportive of Huang, House and Senate committees have summoned him for testimony. Bipartisan legislative efforts to restrict advanced semiconductor access to China are advancing, with Nvidia now in a weaker lobbying position. Analyst Diana Choyleva argues the scandal accelerates what Enodo Economics called the 'Great Decoupling,' though complete technological separation remains difficult given intertwined ecosystems.
items.title: Jensen Huang Scandal May Accelerate US-China Tech Decoupling

items.summary: Police in Paris issued a five-day ban on unauthorized gatherings within 100m of 10 secondary schools and five universities from November 16 to 20, citing disruptions and persistent violence. Some 1,548 people have been arrested since protests began in September over school conditions before spreading nationwide. On Saturday, 106,000 protested across France including 24,000 in Paris, though turnout fell sharply from prior days.
items.title: Paris Police Ban Protests Near Schools and Universities Amid Ongoing Blockades

items.summary: Foreign ministers of Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom and Italy issued a joint statement urging Israel to permit 150,000 tents and vital supplies held at the border into Gaza before winter fully sets in. They described conditions on the ground as dire amid recent floods that left tens of thousands without shelter after deadly storms killed at least four Palestinian children and women. The ministers called for immediate humanitarian access across all crossings, respect for a ceasefire, and implementation of international law obligations.
items.title: Australia, UK, Canada and Italy urge Israel to allow critical aid to Gaza ahead of winter

items.summary: Estonia will close all three of its border crossings with Russia from 1 December following a suspected sabotage attack over the weekend on Threod Systems, a defence company making long-range drones. Authorities attribute it to Russia's GRU and link it to Estonia's support for Ukraine; PM Kristen Michal said preparedness paid off after security agencies warned businesses.
items.title: Estonia Closes All Russia Border Crossings After Suspected GRU Sabotage on Drone Maker

items.summary: President Trump is set to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit this week in Shenzhen, China. The meeting will also include Russian President Vladimir Putin as part of the broader APEC gathering.
items.title: What to Expect from Trump and Xi's Upcoming Meeting in China

items.summary: An NPR investigation reframes the debate over American Eagle's 'Sydney Sweeney Has Great Jeans' campaign by focusing on the garment workers who make those jeans. In Karachi, Pakistan and Dhaka, Bangladesh — two of the world's largest production hubs outside China — reporters interviewed about 20 workers across five factories, including Artistic Garment Industries (which makes for American Eagle) and MBM (Levi's). Workers describe sweltering conditions: temperatures up to 106 F outdoors with factory interiors even hotter; wages around $140–$144 a month; production targets like stitching 200 sleeves an hour or inspecting thousands of pieces daily. They report fainting, heat illness and dehydration while being pressured not to drink water or use the bathroom. Experts from Cornell's Global Labor Institute and Climate Rights International link rising heat to climate change and brands' demand for high volumes on thin margins. Brands like H&M cite corrective action plans; Artistic Garment Industries contests allegations.
items.title: The Workers Behind Sydney Sweeney's Jeans

items.summary: Eight years ago, Lei Yuxi launched a one-person company in Shenzhen with the goal of making sustainable materials commercially viable. After navigating an emerging industry for years, she believes these materials are now on the cusp of a breakthrough. Her ambition goes further: she ultimately wants to eliminate her business's reliance on unnecessary practices entirely.
items.title: Lei Yuxi's Shenzhen Sustainability Venture Aims to Make Sustainability the New Normal

items.summary: Chinese Premier Li Qiang's visit to Manila underscored deepening China-ASEAN economic integration ahead of the 29th China-ASEAN Summit. The bloc recorded $1.15 trillion in two-way trade last year, with ASEAN as its largest partner for six consecutive years and vice versa for 17. Trade grew 24.2% in the first ten months—outpacing overall Chinese foreign trade of 20%. Cumulative investment exceeded $515 billion. Infrastructure projects exemplify cooperation: the China-Laos Railway carried over 73 million passengers, Indonesia's Jakarta-Bandung high-speed rail cut a three-hour journey to 46 minutes at 99.4% on-time performance, and Malaysia's East Coast Rail Link is set for commercial service in January 2027.
items.title: China-ASEAN Trade and Infrastructure Ties Strengthened at Manila Summit

items.summary: Donald Trump made his first public comments on the weekend's air travel disruptions, blaming the Biden administration for leaving a broken system in place. He called on Congress for additional funding to upgrade America's outdated air traffic control systems. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy warned that thousands more US flights have been cancelled and that travel disruptions would continue for another day.
items.title: Trump Blames Biden for Airline Ground Stop

items.summary: Fed up with a record number of elderly South Australians stuck in hospital awaiting permanent care, the regional town of Loxton has taken matters into its own hands. Resident Sally Goode launched the bi-annual Loxton Aged Care Expo to simplify access, while local government added retirement units and an Ageing Well Strategy. SA Health Minister Blair Boyer commended these efforts but maintained responsibility lies with the Commonwealth.
items.title: Loxton Residents Create Their Own Aged Care Solutions Amid Systemic Crisis

items.summary: At 46, Ronaldinho returned from retirement for Serie C club Ravenna, the team he joined as an investor. He started Sunday's 2-0 derby win over Forli and assisted Giulio Donati's opening goal before being substituted at half-time. The sold-out match drew a media circus, with former teammate Dida visiting him on the pitch.
items.title: Ronaldinho Makes Comeback in Ravenna Derby Win

items.summary: Latin America's tourism boom—South American arrivals up 7% and Central American ones 5% last year, both above the global average—is driving overtourism. Machu Picchu draws up to 5,600 visitors daily, risking UNESCO danger-list status; Ecuador doubled Galapagos entrance fees to $200 in 2024; and Mexico City neighborhoods face rent-driven protests. Experts at ITB Americas say sustainable travel is shifting from niche to mainstream: group sizes are shrinking toward four or five, nature-positive programs like reforestation are rising, and community-based tourism is no longer a niche. Booking.com's survey of 32,000 people across 34 countries found 93% want more sustainable choices, with 53% now aware of tourism's impact on local communities. Funders argue access to financing remains key.
items.title: Sustainable Travel Gains Ground Amid Overtourism Concerns in Latin America

items.summary: Spain's coastguard reported nearly 2,200 migrants arrived at the Canary Islands by boat over two days on Sunday, continuing a surge from West Africa amid a declared migration emergency. Most of these 1,324 people aboard 14 dinghies reached El Hierro, approaching the route's record of 1,461 set in November 2020.
items.title: Nearly 2,200 Migrants Reach Spain's Canary Islands in Two Days

items.summary: Representatives of Hungary's wedding industry raised around 3 million Hungarian Forints (€8,218.18) at the 13th Hungarian Wedding Gala to support the Bethesda Children's Hospital with surgical drills for bone surgery. The event gathered over 400 professionals in Budapest and featured awards across 19 categories. Founder Katalin Landesz explained that cooperation began after a colleague's son was burned, making this the third year of hospital support.
items.title: Hungarian Wedding Gala Raises Funds for Children's Hospital Charity Work

items.summary: A United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan rocket failed shortly after launch from Florida on Sunday, destroying its payload of 40 satellites for Amazon's Leo internet network in the company's first mission failure. The rocket failed roughly 10 minutes after liftoff, and the cause was not immediately clear.
items.title: ULA's Vulcan Rocket Fails After Launch, Destroying Amazon Leo Satellites

items.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday that Nvidia should look beyond the company for a new chief executive after Jensen Huang abruptly stepped down last week amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy. Bessent argued the board needs a dramatic shakeup and urged it to answer export-compliance questions within 10 days; the FT reported the board approached Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas.
items.title: Bessent Urges Nvidia to Seek CEO Outside Company

items.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is weighing a return just days after stepping down following revelations of an affair with Alice Huang, suspected by US authorities of spying for Beijing. Allies are assembling a task force to push for his reinstatement, seeking White House backing, while board members consider other candidates such as Arm's Rene Haas.
items.title: Allies rally behind Jensen Huang amid Nvidia leadership shakeup and China spy scandal

items.summary: The Election Commission of India assured the Supreme Court it will include every eligible citizen in electoral rolls and not prosecute those using Form 6 to restore deleted names. The bench, led by CJI Surya Kant with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, had previously ruled no one faces prosecution for re-entering their name via Form 6 amid voter-deletion petitions in Maharashtra and Delhi.
items.title: Election Commission Assures Supreme Court No Prosecution for Form 6 Re-enrollment; Details Restoration Process

items.summary: IPL founder Lalit Modi announced he received British citizenship at an Oxford Union event, celebrating with family on September 15. While the status does not grant legal immunity under the 1992 India-UK treaty, it may have reduced extradition prospects; deportation is now closed, leaving formal extradition as India's sole route. Modi denies wrongdoing over a Rs 125 crore IPL kickback and claims an Interpol Red Notice was stalled by a political witch-hunt.
items.title: Lalit Modi Obtains British Citizenship Amid Extradition Prospects

items.summary: India has secured an agreement with the United States for preferential market access, with lower import duties than competing countries, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said. The understanding was reached between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Donald Trump when they announced a broad framework for their bilateral trade agreement (BTA). Negotiations are underway to finalise the first phase of the deal.
items.title: 'Preferential trade access already agreed': Piyush Goyal's update on India-US trade deal

items.summary: Jake (Jacob) Leach, now the President and CEO of Dexcom—a roughly $30 billion continuous glucose-monitoring company—credits his rise purely to hard work. Born in California's San Fernando Valley, he saved for a $350 bike as a child, worked a $10-an-hour job washing lab glassware at MiniMed (acquired by Medtronic in 2001), and attended UCLA on electrical and biomedical engineering before becoming the first college graduate in his family. In 2004 he joined the 30-person startup Dexcom, nearly doubling his salary from $45,000 to $95,000; over his 22-year tenure there he never asked for a promotion.
items.title: Jake Leach's Rise from Lab Dishwasher to $30B CEO of Dexcom

items.summary: A German cargo and freight services major reported that regional disruption has strained global supply chains, with India-Europe trade among the most affected due to higher freight costs, container shortages and congestion at alternative ports. Even if the Strait of Hormuz reopens, Maier said imbalances in container flows will take time to resolve. DHL's top executive estimated it takes three to six months for the global supply chain to return to normal after a major disruption.
items.title: Global Supply Chains May Take Months to Normalise After Strait of Hormuz Disruption
